Denied service: ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888
Date of denial notice: 2026-08-18
Appeal deadline: 2027-02-14

To the Appeals and Grievances Department:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for ACL reconstruction (CPT 29888), as described in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-18, Reference Number POC-A0C827A88A-54850. The stated reason for denial was that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity." The notice did not quote, attach, or cite the specific medical-necessity criteria (policy title, policy number, or version) that was applied to reach this conclusion, so I am unable to quote or respond point-by-point to plan language here. I am not quoting any plan document in this letter because none was provided to me or located in a publicly available, citable form; any argument below is made in my own words based on the clinical record.

As part of this appeal, I formally request that Meridian/Ambetter from Meridian provide, in writing, the complete text and citation (title, edition/version, and date) of the specific criteria — whether a Meridian/Ambetter clinical policy or an InterQual® module — that was used to deny this request, so that my surgeon and I can respond to it directly if further review is needed.

Without that citation available to me, I ask that the following clinical findings, all contained in the prior authorization packet already submitted by Dr. Duval, be considered in support of medical necessity for arthroscopically aided ACL reconstruction:

1. Confirmed structural injury: MRI of the knee performed 2026-06-22 shows a complete mid-substance tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with an associated bone bruise pattern. The menisci are intact and there is no significant arthritis.

2. Functional instability: I have experienced recurrent instability with pivoting activities and have had my knee give way twice on stairs, indicating that the ligament injury is functionally significant and not merely an incidental imaging finding.

3. Positive physical examination findings: Provocative testing on the affected side was positive, and range of motion is limited by pain, consistent with a clinically significant ACL deficiency.

4. Chronicity: Symptoms have been present and progressive for 9 months, unrelieved by rest.

5. Documented failure of conservative management:
   - Supervised physical therapy for range of motion and quadriceps strengthening, with bracing, over 8 weeks (2026-05-21 to 2026-07-16), with 20 visits completed, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note, without resolution of instability.
   - NSAID therapy for 6 months with inadequate relief.
   - A corticosteroid injection administered 2026-05-07, which provided only 4 weeks of partial relief.

6. No contraindications to surgery: There is no active infection and no untreated substance use disorder. BMI is 29. I am a non-smoker.

Taken together, this record documents a symptomatic, imaging-confirmed complete ACL tear with functional instability that has not responded to a full course of conservative treatment (physical therapy, bracing, NSAIDs, and injection), which is the type of clinical picture generally recognized as supporting surgical reconstruction. I ask that this appeal be reviewed against whatever specific criteria the plan applied, and that the criteria be shared with me and my surgeon, Dr. Duval, so that any remaining gap between the record and the criteria can be identified and addressed.

I request that this appeal be treated as a standard internal appeal and resolved within the timeframe required under the plan's appeal procedures. If my condition worsens or instability episodes increase in frequency before a decision is issued, I reserve the right to request expedited/urgent review.

Enclosed/attached for your reference:
- MRI report dated 2026-06-22
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-21 to 2026-07-16, 20 visits)
- Documentation of corticosteroid injection dated 2026-05-07 and NSAID trial
- Office notes from Dr. Duval, including physical examination findings
- [Copy of original prior authorization request and denial notice]

Please confirm receipt of this appeal in writing and provide the name, credentials, and specialty of the reviewer(s) who will evaluate it. If this internal appeal is not resolved in my favor, please advise me of the process and deadline for requesting an external review through the Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services under the Patient's Right to Independent Review Act.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Riley Hayes
Member ID: W842220872
